name: swarm
description: Handle a request, delegating independent testable subtasks to the swarm (worker models in git worktrees)
author: ooChat
prompt_template:
Handle the request below. Consider delegating parts of it to the swarm: worker models that execute small tasks in isolated git worktrees until an acceptance command passes. You direct the swarm by running `swarm` CLI commands with the run_shell tool, from the repository root.

## Decide first
Use the swarm when the work splits into independent, testable tasks: the same change across many files, many small fixes each with a test, tests/docstrings/type hints per module, or reading lots of code for reviews and inventories (report tasks). Do the work yourself when it is small, one coupled design change, when a task spec would be as long as the code, or when the location of a bug is unknown (workers cannot explore or run commands). State your decision and why in one or two sentences. If you decide against the swarm, just do the request.

## If using the swarm
1. Run `swarm guide` and follow it; it is the authoritative contract. The steps below are a summary.
2. `swarm status`. If it shows no live workers, stop and ask the user to start some (`swarm work -p <profile>` in a terminal; `swarm profiles` lists profiles).
3. `swarm init` if `.swarm/` does not exist. Tasks start from HEAD: if the work tree has uncommitted changes the tasks need, ask the user before committing.
4. Write one `.swarm/tasks/<ID>/task.yaml` per task (fields: id, goal, write_scope, read, acceptance, depends_on, notes, budget; report tasks use `kind: report` and no write_scope/acceptance). Put excerpts workers need in `.swarm/tasks/<ID>/context/`. Workers see only what you give them: exact names, signatures, paths, current errors. One behavior per task. Concurrent tasks need disjoint write_scope; otherwise order them with depends_on. Acceptance must print what it checks when it fails and must not use fixed shared paths or ports. budget.context_tokens must fit the workers' max_prompt.
5. `swarm validate --dry-run`: every acceptance must fail on the base because the work is not done yet, not because the command is broken. Fix checks whose reason is wrong.
6. Wait with `swarm wait --timeout 50` (the shell tool times out at 60s); repeat until tasks finish. Do not poll other ways, tail logs, or read worker terminals.
7. For finished tasks: `swarm review ID...`. Correct -> `swarm merge ID`. Wrong or failed -> `swarm reset --hold ID`, add the missing fact or error to notes/context, `swarm release ID`. Badly specified -> `swarm delete ID` and write a new task. Report findings are leads: verify before acting on them.
8. When everything is merged, run the project's real build/tests yourself and turn failures into new small tasks or fix them directly.

End with a short summary: what was delegated, what you did yourself, what was merged, and anything left open.

## Request
{{input}}
input_hint: Describe the work, e.g. "add type hints to every module in modules/"
